newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end sharply lower on Kia, shooting.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end sharply lower on Kia, shooting.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed sharply lower on Wednesday as troubles with the Kia Group hammered shares of the financial sector and Kia companies, brokers said.
The news of an exchange of fire between South and North Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone added selling pressure in the afternoon, they said.
The composite stock index ended 2.03 percent or 15.33 points lower at 739.72.
"Banks took the most severe beating today because of the sheer size of their loans to Kia," said Yoo Bong-keun, a broker at LG Securities.
The sub-index for the banking sector fell 5.83 percent to 341.21, and the index for the whole financial sector dropped 5.21 percent to 531.28.
Korea First Bank, a leading creditor of the Kia Group, fell 280 won to its daily lower limit of 3,220.
"Financial shares would remain the weakest sector as long as Kia woes were lingering," said Na Min-ho of Daishin Securities.
The Kia Group had total loans of 9.54 trillion won at the end of May, of which 5.48 trillion won were borrowed from banks, according to Korea First Bank figures.
Korea First's loans to Kia totalled 814.2 billion won.
All of Kia's six listed companies fell to their limit-lows. The group's flagship carmaker Kia Motors dropped 1,000 won to its limit of 12,400.
Kia's commercial vehicle unit Asia Motors fell 280 won to its limit of 3,270.

Seoul's defence ministry officials said North Korea launched artillery shells at a Southern border post this morning during a fierce exchange of fire this morning, describing the incident as a "serious provocation."
North Korea in a Pyongyang radio broadcast accused the South of a "grave military provocation act."
